# #147 - Det blev ett fjestober för Stockholmsbörsen och ett skräcktober för Nasdaq 100

**Feed**: montrosepodden  
**Published**: 2026-11-06  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

The hosts look back on October 2026. OMXS30 rose just 0.07% for the month, the weakest positive October on record, while Nasdaq 100 fell 6.66% and ended with a sharp sell-off on Friday. Their main question is whether anything has changed apart from sentiment. They answer no: Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta all report strong AI and cloud demand, capacity limits, rising GPU rental prices and high cloud margins, and US tech now trades at its lowest P/E in five years. They also cover the Democratic midterm sweep, a possible Texas datacenter moratorium, Alphabet's first negative free cash flow, Intel's weak PC guidance and AMD's strong report, and they expect a solid year-end rally.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 GOOGL — Alphabet | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Cloud +103% with margin up to 36%, Gemini 1B users, full-stack AI and TPU sales; P/E 14.4 trailing, ~15.8 in 2028; hosts believe Google will handle the search disruption.

#### Reasoning

Hosts say the market's worry about Alphabet's negative FCF and search cannibalization overlooks very profitable cloud growth, record query growth, YouTube/Maps data and full-stack moats. Valuation looks undemanding versus Axfood and Telia. They point out they were right a year ago when the market feared ChatGPT would kill Google.

#### Sell Triggers

- if ChatGPT search share keeps rising and erodes Google ad pricing
- if AI capex fails to earn returns and FCF stays negative
- if US regulators force a breakup

> *"Jag tror ändå att Google kommer att lösa det här."*

---

### 🟡 NVDA — Nvidia | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

No company near Nvidia on performance; GPU rental prices rising even for old chips; demand exceeds supply; custom ASIC/TPU competition is a risk.

#### Reasoning

Host sees Nvidia as best in class (Ferrari V8 vs a vacuum-cleaner motor) and points to rising GPU prices and SpaceX going all-in as signs of strong demand. Hyperscaler custom silicon is a stated worry, but there is no explicit buy call.

#### Sell Triggers

- if custom TPUs/ASICs take significant share
- if GPU rental prices start falling
- if hyperscaler capex slows

> *"det finns ju ingen som ens är i närheten av Nvidia när det kommer till prestanda"*

---

### ⛔ INTC — Intel | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 45%

Worst day since 1974 (-28.55%), soft PC guidance, can't meet datacenter demand, fatal fab explosion in Israel; unclear if rally was on own merits.

#### Reasoning

Hosts call it a 'bad cocktail': the PC market is cooling on high memory prices and it can't capture record datacenter demand because of supply problems. They question whether past gains came from Trump/government support rather than its own execution ('the proof is in the pudding').

#### Sell Triggers

- if Intel shows it can meet datacenter CPU demand
- if PC market demand recovers

> *"Som också gör att det blir ju motvind, en dålig cocktail för bolaget."*

---

### 🟠 AMD — AMD | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Very strong report and rally; CPU demand rising as AI moves from training to inference (GPU:CPU ratio from 10:1 toward 1:1); capacity-limited.

#### Reasoning

Hosts highlight AMD's surge in demand and see it as a beneficiary of more CPUs per GPU in inference, while Intel struggles. It was also among the worst performers in the Friday sell-off despite being +136% YTD, so it is volatile.

#### Sell Triggers

- if inference CPU demand fails to materialize
- if capacity constraints persist and limit growth

> *"AMD kom med en jättebra rapport. tjurrusning kring efterfrågan."*
